title: Ample invertible module on a scheme (absolute ampleness)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $n\ge0$ write $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ for the $n$-fold tensor product $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\dots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (with $\mathcal L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$), and for a global section $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ put $X_s=\{x\in X:\ s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$, the set of points where the value of $s$ in $(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)$ is nonzero ($\kappa(x)$ the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]); it is an open subset of $X$, viewed as an open subscheme. $\mathcal L$ is *ample* if (1) $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (every open covering of the underlying space has a finite subcovering), and (2) for every $x\in X$ there exist $n\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ such that $x\in X_s$ and the open subscheme $X_s$ is affine. This is the absolute notion of Stacks Properties Definition 01PS (EGA II 4.5.3 with criterion 4.5.2 a')); it is not the notion of [def-sc-ample], which is stated only for proper schemes over a field via very ampleness of a power.

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (label definition-ample); EGA II (literature/ega/EGA-II_PMIHES-8-1961.pdf), Définition 4.5.3 with Théorème 4.5.2 a')
